evals.prompt: I'm working on a React 19 + TypeScript + Vite web app for room booking (repo is at C:\dev\roomplanner-web, source in src/). The booking editor (src/features/bookings/BookingEditor.tsx) uses two plain <input type="time"> elements for start and end time and the front desk keeps typing things like 930 or 9.30 and getting garbage or a browser-specific picker. Please build a proper TimeField React component in src/components and use it in the editor instead of the two inputs. People type fast on the keyboard, so it has to feel right without touching the mouse. Our design brief (docs/design.md) says controls are 34 px high, radius 8, Inter font, and the tokens live in src/styles/tokens.css. Add tests too (we use Vitest, Testing Library and Playwright).
evals.expected_output: Finds and follows the project brief and token file (34 px height, radius 8, Inter) and notes where they differ from Fluent defaults (32 px, radius 4) instead of silently using Fluent values. Builds a TimeField on a pure parser module (no React) with a table test via it.each: 9 and 09 give 09:00, 930 and 0930 give 09:30, 9:30 and 9.30 and 9,30 give 09:30, 9:5 gives 09:05, and 24, 9:60 and abc give an error message that names the valid range 00:00 to 23:59. The input is type="text" with inputMode="numeric" (not type="time" or type="number"), autoComplete off, spellCheck false, maxLength 5; onChange only filters characters (digits, colon, dot, comma, at most five) and never reformats while typing. The component holds three things: the raw text, the committed value (prop) and an error. It commits on Enter and on blur, writes HH:mm back, keeps invalid text with aria-invalid="true" and an error message instead of clearing it, and prevents form submit on Enter while invalid. Tab into the field selects all text (fast field), a mouse click places the caret. ArrowUp/ArrowDown step by the configured minute increment, Shift+Arrow one minute, PageUp/PageDown one hour, no wrap past midnight, mouse wheel only while focused. Esc restores the last committed value and stops propagation so the next Esc closes the surrounding dialog; Enter commits and lets the form submit when valid. End-before-start is reported as an error on the end field by the page from committed values, and the end field is only recalculated after commit, not while typing. The field is wrapped in a label (htmlFor/useId), help text, error text with aria-describedby pointing at whichever of help or error is shown, a required marker that is aria-hidden plus aria-required on the control, and no placeholder used as label. Styles come from the token file (no hex in TSX or component CSS; the hex/rgb/named-color/inline-shadow/inline-style ripgrep scans are run), focus is visible after a mouse click (underline on :focus-within that grows about 200 ms and leaves about 50 ms, or an equivalent 2 px ring using :focus-visible), transitions animate color and transform only and honor both prefers-reduced-motion and the app's reduce-motion setting. Tests: Vitest parser table; Testing Library with userEvent.setup() driving real keys (Tab, typing, arrows, Esc, Enter) and querying by role and accessible name, asserting aria-invalid, accessible description and the selected text; a Playwright test with light and dark screenshots via emulateMedia({ colorScheme }), a reduced-motion run via emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' }) that reads getComputedStyle transition-duration, and an axe run with @axe-core/playwright. The final report says what was tested, what was not (no real screen reader pass, jsdom has no layout, other browsers not run), and which deviations from Fluent should be recorded in the project.

evals.prompt: Can you review the text input style in src/index.css (the .field input, .field input:hover and .field input:focus rules) against Fluent 2 and fix what's wrong? We got feedback that you can't tell which field has focus and that the borders look washed out, and our accessibility audit flagged contrast. The brief in docs/design.md says 34 px height and radius 8 and that's intentional. Colors live in src/styles/tokens.css as CSS custom properties with a prefers-color-scheme block and a [data-theme] override.
evals.expected_output: Reads the brief, index.css and the token file first and treats 34 px height and radius 8 as recorded, deliberate deviations (reported as fine, not as findings). Reports findings in a table (finding, rule, fix, status) and does not rewrite unrelated styles. Measures contrast instead of guessing: computes the field border against the surface for light and dark from the resolved token values and notes that a typical light border token is far below 3:1 (Fluent's own default border #d1d1d1 on white is about 1.5:1 and compensates with a darker bottom edge of about 6:1); proposes a darker bottom-edge or border token and shows the measured ratios before and after. Finds the focus problem in the CSS (outline: none or outline: 0 without a replacement, or a focus rule that reuses the hover color) and adds a focus indicator that also shows after a mouse click: a 2 px accent underline on :focus-within via ::after with transform scaleX that grows in about 200 ms and leaves in about 50 ms, or an equivalent 2 px outline with offset on :focus-visible, with a light halo or a system color in @media (forced-colors: active) so it survives forced colors and is visible on every background. Fixes hover, active and disabled states using selectors in the stylesheet, not inline style attributes; checks that :hover does not reuse the rest color; looks for cascade causes (rule order, specificity, @layer, an inline style in the TSX) when a rule has no effect. Removes hard-coded hex and color functions in favor of var(--token) with scans for hex, rgb/hsl, named colors, inline box-shadow and style={{ }} colors, keeps label and help text readable when the field is disabled (disabled look on the input, not on the container), lists the transition properties (no transition: all, no layout properties) and adds the prefers-reduced-motion block plus the in-app class. Placeholder contrast is checked (about 4.5:1) via ::placeholder. Error state uses [aria-invalid="true"] with the danger color plus an icon and message text, not color alone. Verifies with Playwright screenshots per state in light and dark (emulateMedia colorScheme, forcedColors) and a computed-style contrast check, runs axe on the page, and lists what could not be verified (for example behavior at browser zoom 200 percent, real Windows high contrast themes, other browsers, a screen reader).

evals.prompt: In our React 19 app (src/features/inbox) I need to add a panel to InboxView.tsx that shows an AI-written draft reply for the selected customer message, with Send, Edit and Discard buttons. The draft comes from a useDraft(messageId) hook that wraps our draft API. The panel sits in the right-hand side panel next to the message list. We use Fluent UI React v9 (@fluentui/react-components) with a FluentProvider. Please build it so it's properly labeled as AI and users stay in control. If the draft service is unavailable (no API key set or request failed) the panel should say so sensibly.
evals.expected_output: Builds the panel in the existing side-panel pattern using the project's tokens and Fluent UI React v9 components inside the FluentProvider (Button with appearance, MessageBar, Field, Textarea) without a second style system. Marks every AI spot with a consistent small AI badge and an icon instead of a face or human name, shows the approved disclaimer line under the draft (wording kept in one central message table) and a clear status such as 'AI draft, not sent yet'. Drafts are never sent automatically: Send requires a visible review step (a confirm dialog or an explicit review state) and is a verb-based primary button; Edit turns the text into an ordinary editable multi-line Textarea in a Field with a label, with the right keyboard behavior (Enter newline, Ctrl+Enter sends, Esc handled and does not discard silently); Discard and an Undo path (toast or inline) exist. Includes a collapsible 'Why this suggestion?' section built as a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls (or Accordion), listing sources or rules, and two neutral feedback buttons (helpful, not helpful) with categories on 'not helpful'. Tone of any AI-generated strings is factual with no first-person feelings. Unavailable and failure states explain why and how to fix it and give two ways forward, one of them without AI ('Write the reply yourself'), as a MessageBar with intent error or warning inside a polite or assertive live region as appropriate (role alert for errors, role status for the loading text 'Writing draft...'); the live region container exists before its text changes; the retry button is a real button. There is a per-function setting to switch the feature off and a first-use explainer. Adds accessible names (no icon-only button without aria-label), a defined focus order that equals DOM order, focus restoration to the invoker after the review dialog or panel closes, a visible :focus-visible ring, and tests: Testing Library with userEvent for no send without user action, failure state with a non-AI path, AI badge present, keyboard paths (Tab order, Ctrl+Enter, Esc) and role/name queries; Playwright with axe (@axe-core/playwright) over the inbox route as the owner role, a light and dark screenshot, and a prefers-reduced-motion run. The report scores or at least walks the Responsible AI rubric and states what was not checked (screen reader pass, real service errors, other browsers).
